symbols.name: G
symbols.def: The even first-stage randomization size in each block.

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: The number of sequential assignment blocks.

symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The fixed number of units in each group.

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: A fixed bound for every potential endpoint.

symbols.name: K_H
symbols.def: A fixed bound for the centered group scores.

symbols.name: c_\sigma
symbols.def: A constant independent of \(G\), \(B\), the block, and the realized history.

symbols.name: C_\sigma
symbols.def: A constant independent of \(G\), \(B\), the block, and the realized history.

symbols.name: c_\rho
symbols.def: A constant controlling the joint growth of groups and blocks.

symbols.name: C_\rho
symbols.def: A constant controlling the joint growth of groups and blocks.

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: The fixed penalty on squared standardized imbalance.

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: The prespecified level for simultaneous inference.

symbols.name: \mathcal H_t
symbols.type: within-group treatment-and-saturation history space through time \(t\)
symbols.def: The history records own-treatment and group-saturation exposures through period \(t\).

symbols.name: \mathcal H_{2B}
symbols.def: The history records own-treatment and group-saturation exposures over all \(2B\) experimental periods.

symbols.name: Y_{gti}
symbols.def: The endpoint response of unit \(i\) in group \(g\) at time \(t\) under a complete within-group exposure path.

symbols.name: Y_{gbi}(d,q)
symbols.def: \(Y_{gbi}(d,q)=Y_{g,2b,i}(h)\) for any \(h\in\mathcal H_{2B}\) whose entries at periods \(2b-1\) and \(2b\) both equal \((d,q)\); ordinary nonanticipation and the imposed lag-one finite-memory restriction make this value invariant to the remaining entries.

symbols.name: \mathcal F_b
symbols.def: \(\mathcal F_b\) is generated by assignments and observed endpoints through block \(b\).

symbols.name: \bar Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_{gb}
symbols.type: observed group mean at block endpoint

symbols.name: \bar Y^{\mathrm{obs}}_b
symbols.type: observed grand group mean at block endpoint

symbols.name: H_g
symbols.def: A prespecified centered group covariate score.

symbols.name: A_{gbi}
symbols.def: Conditionally on \(x_b\), exactly \(nQ_{gb}\) units are sampled uniformly without replacement in group \(g\), independently across groups, and assigned treatment one at both periods of block \(b\); the remaining units receive zero.

symbols.name: \pi_{k\ell,b}
symbols.def: For exposure cells \(k\) and \(\ell\) in block \(b\), \(\pi_{k\ell,b}=\Pr(I_kI_\ell=1\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})\), with \(\pi_{kk,b}=\pi_{k,b}\); these known probabilities are logged by the randomizer.

symbols.name: \tau_b
symbols.def: \(\tau_b=(Gn)^{-1}\sum_{g,i,d,q}c_{dq}Y_{gbi}(d,q)\), where the sums range over \(\mathcal G_G\), \(\mathcal I_n\), \(\mathcal D\), and \(\mathcal Q\).

symbols.name: A_b
symbols.type: balanced-sign component of the block score

symbols.name: U_b
symbols.type: within-group component of the block score

symbols.name: (A_b^\star,W_b^\star)
symbols.def: A centered Gaussian vector with the exact conditional \(P_0\)-covariance of \((A_b,W_b)\), supported on that covariance range when singular.

symbols.name: (R_b^\star,W_b^\star)
symbols.def: A centered Gaussian vector with the exact conditional \(P_0\)-covariance of \((R_b,W_b)\), supported on that covariance range when singular.

symbols.name: \mathcal K_b
symbols.def: Each \(k=(g,i,d,q)\in\mathcal K_b\) indexes one potential exposure cell in block \(b\).

symbols.name: \widehat\Gamma_b
symbols.def: The pairwise Horvitz--Thompson covariance sum augmented by a diagonal positive-semidefinite completion for \(\mathcal Z_b\).

assumptions.condition: Conditional on the finite population \(\{Y_{gti}:g\in\mathcal G_G,\ i\in\mathcal I_n\}\), the only randomness is generated by \(x_b\) and \(A_{gbi}\).
For every unit, \(Y_{gti}\) is invariant to treatment and saturation assignments outside group \(g\).
Within group \(g\), the endpoint response depends on the contemporaneous assignment vector only through the unit's own treatment \(d\) and the realized saturation \(q\).
For every \(t\leq2B\), if \(h,h'\in\mathcal H_{2B}\) agree through period \(t\), then \(Y_{gti}(h)=Y_{gti}(h')\); assignments after period \(t\) do not affect the period-\(t\) endpoint.
For every \(2\leq t\leq2B\), if \(h,h'\in\mathcal H_{2B}\) agree at periods \(t-1\) and \(t\), then \(Y_{gti}(h)=Y_{gti}(h')\) regardless of the remaining history entries.

novel.justification: This is an imposed finite-memory restriction, not a consequence of ordinary nonanticipation. It is interpretable when saturation and own treatment are held fixed within each two-period block, so the endpoint depends on the block's sustained exposure while earlier blocks may affect the predictable randomization rule but not the endpoint response.

assumptions.condition: Uniformly over \(b\in\mathcal B_B\) and realized \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\), \(c_\sigma\leq\sigma_b^2\leq C_\sigma\).

definitions.name: bounded lag-one partial-interference triangular-array class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{G,B}=\{(Y,H):G\in2\mathbb N,\ B\in\mathbb N,\ n\in4\mathbb N,\ \text{assumptions }\texttt{ass:design-based-finiteness},\texttt{ass:partial-interference},\texttt{ass:stratified-interference},\texttt{ass:nonanticipation},\texttt{ass:finite-memory-lag-one},\texttt{ass:imbalance-variance-window},\texttt{ass:joint-growth},\texttt{ass:rr-covariance-stabilization},\texttt{ass:rr-limit-positive},\texttt{ass:cr-covariance-stabilization},\texttt{ass:projection-stabilization}\text{ hold}\}\).

definitions.name: predictable complement-symmetric soft rerandomization
definitions.construction: At block \(b\), draw \(x_b\in\mathcal X_G\) with \(P_{\mathrm{RR},b}(x\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=P_0(x)f_{\eta,\kappa}\{W_b(x)\}/C_b\); set \(Q_{gb}=q_H\) for \(x_{gb}=1\) and \(q_L\) otherwise; then draw exactly \(nQ_{gb}\) treated units uniformly and independently within each group and hold both stages fixed for the two periods.

definitions.name: perfect-matching handle for singular weighted Gaussian transport
definitions.construction: Represent the balanced three-vector \((a_{gb,1},a_{gb,2},V_{gb}/\sigma_b)\) by a uniform random perfect matching followed by independent pair orientations; target a history-uniform covariance-range comparison through smooth Lindeberg replacement, covariance interpolation, fourth-moment truncation, and a conditional characteristic-function augmentation for \(U_b\).

definitions.name: observable positive-semidefinite completed covariance estimator
definitions.construction: \(\widehat\Gamma_b=(Gn^2)^{-1}[\sum_{k,\ell:\pi_{k\ell,b}>0}I_kI_\ell(\pi_{k\ell,b}-\pi_{k,b}\pi_{\ell,b})u_{k,b}u_{\ell,b}^\top/(\pi_{k\ell,b}\pi_{k,b}\pi_{\ell,b})+\sum_{\{k,\ell\}\in\mathcal Z_b}\{I_ku_{k,b}u_{k,b}^\top/\pi_{k,b}+I_\ell u_{\ell,b}u_{\ell,b}^\top/\pi_{\ell,b}\}]\), followed by block averaging and eigenvalue clipping at \(r_B\).

definitions.name: alternating-block genuinely adaptive finite-population witness
definitions.construction: For \(G\in4\mathbb N\), represent the four sign pairs \((H_g,J_g)\in\{-1,1\}^2\) equally often and set \(\lambda=1\). On type A blocks take \((a_{Dg},a_{Sg})=(H_g,J_g)\) and \(L=0\); on type B blocks take \((a_{Dg},a_{Sg})=(J_g,H_g)\) and \(L=4\). Set \(\theta_g=4a_{Dg}\), \(\delta_g=L-\theta_g\), \(h_g=a_{Sg}/2+a_{Dg}-L/2\), and \(Y_{gbi}(d,q)=h_g+d(\delta_g+\theta_gq)\).

statements.statement: For every finite \(G\), \(B\), and history, complement symmetry gives \(\Pr_{\mathrm{RR}}(Q_{gb}=q_H\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=\Pr_{\mathrm{RR}}(Q_{gb}=q_L\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=1/2\). Hence \(\pi_{gbi,dq}=p_{dq}/2\geq1/8\) and \(\mathbb E_{\mathrm{RR}}(\widehat\tau)=\tau\) exactly.
statements.justification: Exact first-order symmetry prevents adaptive normalizers from creating bias or hidden first-order weights.
statements.gap: YuMaLiu2025 Theorem 3 treats a fixed minimax two-stage design, while LiZhao2026Adaptive Theorem 1 treats single-stage logged propensities; neither proves this two-stage complement-symmetric adaptive identity.
statements.consumer: A prospective multigroup market experiment can log the adaptive kernel and retain an exactly interpretable joint sustained-exposure target.

statements.statement: For every block, \(R_b=A_b+U_b\), \(\mathbb E(U_b\mid x_b,\mathcal F_{b-1})=0\), and the group summands of \(U_b\) are conditionally independent. Consequently \(\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}=\operatorname{Var}_{\mathrm{RR}}(A_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})+K_b\), the cross covariance is zero, and exactly the same \(K_b\) appears under \(P_0\).
statements.justification: This exact split isolates the only covariance component that the first-stage soft tilt can change.
statements.gap: JiangImaiMalani2023 derives static two-stage covariance formulas, but not this predictable balanced-sign decomposition with unchanged fixed-count within-group covariance.
statements.consumer: The decomposition is the algebraic bridge from the adaptive design to the projection-efficiency theorem and the observable studentizer.

statements.statement: The block scores satisfy \(\mathbb E(R_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=0\), and \(\sqrt{GB}(\widehat\tau-\tau)=B^{-1/2}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_B}R_b\).
statements.justification: Predictable centering makes the across-block accumulation a design-based martingale rather than a pseudo-target drift.
statements.gap: LiZhao2026Adaptive supplies the single-stage martingale template, while the present score has dependent two-stage exposure categories and lagged potential outcomes.
statements.consumer: This identity supplies the filtration structure needed for the root-\(GB\) limit law.

statements.statement: There exists a finite constant \(C_R\), independent of \(G\), \(B\), \(b\), and the history, such that \(\mathbb E_0\|R_b\|^4\leq C_R\) and \(\mathbb E_{\mathrm{RR}}(\|R_b\|^4\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})\leq C_R/\eta\).
statements.justification: The uniform fourth moment supplies the actual conditional Lindeberg control rather than treating covariance stabilization as a substitute.
statements.gap: LiDing2017FPCLT gives finite-population leverage conditions, but not likelihood-ratio transfer of a joint two-stage score under a predictable soft tilt.
statements.consumer: The martingale central limit theorem uses this bound to control every Cram\'er--Wold contrast.

statements.statement: Does there exist a deterministic \(\varepsilon_G\downarrow0\) such that, uniformly over blocks, histories, and members of \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\), \[\left|\mathbb E_0f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)-\mathbb Ef_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b^\star)\right|+\left\|\mathbb E_0[A_bA_b^\top f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)]-\mathbb E[A_b^\star A_b^{\star\top}f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b^\star)]\right\|\leq\varepsilon_G,\] and, after adding the conditionally centered fixed-count noise, \[\left\|\mathbb E_0[R_bR_b^\top f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)]-\mathbb E[R_b^\star R_b^{\star\top}f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b^\star)]\right\|\leq\varepsilon_G?\] The claim must hold on the covariance range when the score covariance is singular, without a smallest-eigenvalue condition on the two score coordinates.
statements.justification: Ordinary weak convergence does not transport the unbounded quadratic score moment that determines the selected-design covariance.
statements.gap: ShiDing2026BerryEsseen Theorem 1 and its quadratic-form results require nonsingular standardization, while TianYangDing2025 treats scalar stratified linear statistics; neither gives predictable radial weighting or singular-support second-moment transport.
statements.consumer: A positive answer closes the covariance calculation needed for every contrast-specific precision guarantee under the adaptive saturation design.

statements.statement: There is a constant \(C_\pi<\infty\), independent of block and history, such that for distinct groups \(g\neq h\), \(\left|\mathbb E_{\mathrm{RR}}(x_{gb}x_{hb}\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})\right|\leq C_\pi/G\). Therefore every feasible cross-group exposure-pair probability equals its product-marginal benchmark plus \(O(G^{-1})\) uniformly, while every feasible within-group pair probability is bounded away from zero.
statements.justification: Uniform pair control turns the exact PSD completion identity into a concentrating observable matrix estimator.
statements.gap: Static two-stage variance papers compute pair probabilities directly; predictable soft weighting requires a new mixed finite-difference bound under the fixed-half support.
statements.consumer: The bound controls the \(O(G^2)\) cross-group terms in the conservative covariance estimator.

statements.statement: Uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\), \[\sqrt{GB}(\widehat\tau-\tau)=B^{-1/2}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_B}R_b\ \Rightarrow\ N_2(0,\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}).\] The convergence is derived from the randomization filtration and the primitive fourth-moment and predictable-covariance conditions.
statements.justification: The root-\(GB\) joint law is the inferential payoff of combining many randomized groups with repeated predictable blocks.
statements.gap: YuMaLiu2025 proves HT asymptotics for a fixed minimax schedule, and LiZhao2026Adaptive treats general single-stage adaptive scores; neither derives this joint fixed-count spillover-and-carryover martingale law.
statements.consumer: It permits joint direct-and-spillover uncertainty quantification in prospective multigroup online experiments.

statements.statement: Uniformly over blocks and histories, \(\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}=\Sigma_{b,0}-(1-v_{\eta,\kappa})\beta_b\beta_b^\top+o(1)\). Consequently \[\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{CR}}-(1-v_{\eta,\kappa})P.\] For every fixed contrast \(c\in\mathbb R^2\setminus\{0\}\), soft rerandomization has strictly smaller asymptotic variance than complete randomization if and only if \(c^\top Pc>0\).
statements.justification: The identity names the exact precision gain and characterizes all and only the improved causal contrasts.
statements.gap: LiDingRubin2018 Theorem 1 gives a static hard-truncation scalar ATE decomposition; this theorem targets a predictable soft tilt, a joint direct-and-spillover vector, fixed-half group saturations, and unchanged second-stage sampling noise.
statements.consumer: The population criterion classifies which scientifically chosen direct-spillover contrasts gain asymptotic precision in theoretical design comparisons and fully specified simulation calibrations.

statements.statement: For every block, \(\mathbb E(\widehat\Gamma_b\mid\mathcal F_{b-1})=\Sigma_{b,\mathrm{RR}}+D_b\) with \(D_b\succeq0\). Moreover \[\widehat\Gamma=\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}+B^{-1}\sum_{b\in\mathcal B_B}D_b+o_P(1),\] so every subsequential limit of \(\widehat\Gamma\) dominates \(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}\) in Loewner order and \(\widehat\Gamma_+\) is asymptotically invertible.
statements.justification: The matrix completion handles impossible joint exposure cells without imputing cross-potential-outcome products.
statements.gap: JiangImaiMalani2023 provides conservative covariance estimators for static two-stage designs; the present identity and concentration result cover logged history-dependent pair probabilities and matrix, rather than coordinatewise, conservativeness.
statements.consumer: The completed matrix supports simultaneous inference even when some within-group exposure pairs can never be jointly observed.

statements.justification: Joint coverage, rather than two unadjusted marginal intervals, is the operational inferential guarantee.
statements.gap: YuMaLiu2025 reports marginal conservative intervals under its fixed design, while the present result uses a history-dependent design and a positive-semidefinite completed \(2\)-by-\(2\) covariance matrix.
statements.consumer: Market experimenters obtain one simultaneous region for sustained direct and saturation-spillover effects.

statements.statement: On the boundary extension \(\eta=1\), or equivalently when \(\kappa=0\), \(f_{\eta,\kappa}\equiv1\), \(P_{\mathrm{RR},b}=P_0\), \(v_{\eta,\kappa}=1\), and \(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{CR}}\); the estimator and studentizer reduce to the ordinary balanced two-stage Horvitz--Thompson construction.
statements.justification: The reduction checks that the new design nests its complete-randomization benchmark without altering the causal target.
statements.gap: This is a required sanity reduction rather than a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: Implementers can recover the familiar design by switching off the soft balance penalty.

statements.statement: The family \(\mathcal W^{AB}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{G,B}\), its type A and type B imbalance variances converge to \(53/16\) and \(29/16\), and \[P=\frac12\left\{\frac1{53}\begin{pmatrix}36&6\\6&1\end{pmatrix}+\frac1{29}\begin{pmatrix}4&10\\10&25\end{pmatrix}\right\}\succ0.\] Thus the design is genuinely adaptive through prior observed outcomes and every nonzero joint contrast is strictly improved.
statements.justification: A heterogeneous alternating projection witness establishes that the gain need not be rank one after aggregation and that adaptation is not cosmetic.
statements.gap: Static cluster rerandomization examples use fixed covariates and a fixed projection direction; this family alternates two outcome-adaptive directions while retaining one universal standardized tilt constant.
statements.consumer: It gives simulation designers a falsifiable benchmark whose covariance gain is positive for every direct-spillover contrast.

sampling_model.design: At each block, condition on \(\mathcal F_{b-1}\), softly tilt the uniform fixed-half saturation assignment by \(f_{\eta,\kappa}(W_b)\), then use independent fixed-count randomization within groups and hold both assignments for two periods.
sampling_model.units: The finite population consists of \(G\) mutually isolated groups of fixed size \(n\), observed at the endpoints of \(B\) two-period blocks; potential outcomes are fixed.
sampling_model.treatment: The first stage assigns exactly \(G/2\) groups to each of \(q_L=1/4\) and \(q_H=3/4\); the second stage treats exactly \(nq\) units within a group assigned saturation \(q\).
sampling_model.overlap: Complement symmetry gives first-stage probability \(1/2\), so every exposure cell has conditional probability \(p_{dq}/2\geq1/8\); feasible pair probabilities are logged and impossible within-group pairs receive PSD completion.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No superpopulation nuisance is estimated. The randomizer records exact conditional first- and second-order inclusion probabilities, and the analysis uses only observed exposure-cell outcomes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorems 1--2 characterize a fixed minimax two-stage spillover-and-carryover design, and the later inference results establish Horvitz--Thompson asymptotics under that design.
Theorems 1--2 give finite-population IPW unbiasedness and a martingale central limit theorem under general single-stage adaptive probabilities.
Theorem 1 decomposes the static hard-rerandomization ATE limit into an unaffected Gaussian residual and a truncated Gaussian covariate projection.
Theorems 1--3 provide unbiased joint two-stage effect estimators and conservative randomization covariance formulas under a static design.
The paper derives Berry--Esseen bounds for linear and quadratic functions of standardized permutation estimators.
The paper gives Stein-coupling Berry--Esseen bounds for heterogeneous stratified linear permutation statistics.
The paper establishes asymptotic inference for static two-stage covariate-adaptive randomization under partial interference.
The paper gives broad two-stage interference estimators, central limit theorems, and conservative variance procedures without requiring exposure mappings.
The paper develops exact and asymptotically valid randomization tests for static randomized saturation designs.
The paper constructs Gaussian-prepivoted tests that are exact under sharp nulls and asymptotically valid under weak nulls, including static rerandomized designs.

tldr: Predictable soft rerandomization can balance lagged group outcomes without changing the joint sustained direct-and-spillover target. Complement symmetry gives exact first-order propensities, an exact score split isolates the rerandomized balanced-sign component, and a history-uniform singular-support Gaussian transport result would yield both the root-\(GB\) joint limit and the covariance identity \(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{CR}}-(1-v_{\eta,\kappa})P\). Logged pair probabilities and a PSD completion produce an observable conservative \(2\)-by-\(2\) studentizer and simultaneous Wald coverage.

project_justification.gap: Existing papers separately cover static spillover-and-carryover design, sequential balance, general adaptive IPW martingales, and static rerandomization projection geometry. None supplies the history-uniform soft-tilt quadratic-moment transport that joins these layers under fixed-half group saturations and fixed-count within-group assignment.
project_justification.niche: A predictable complement-symmetric kernel preserves exact joint Horvitz--Thompson identification while allowing prior outcomes to improve the precision of sustained direct and spillover effects.
project_justification.fill: The project derives exact unbiasedness, a two-stage martingale/combinatorial central limit theorem, an observable PSD-conservative matrix studentizer, simultaneous coverage, and an explicit projection covariance gain, with the singular weighted Gaussian approximation exposed as the first open theorem step.

related_work: Hudgens--Halloran (2008) and Jiang--Imai--Malani (2023) define and estimate direct and spillover contrasts under static two-stage partial interference. Bojinov--Rambachan--Shephard (2021) supplies the ordinary no-future-assignment nonanticipation convention for dynamic potential outcomes; the stronger lag-one finite-memory equality used here is an imposed restriction tailored to endpoints after two-period held assignments and is not attributed to that paper. Yu--Ma--Liu (2025) adds carryover and a minimax timing design, but its first-stage law is fixed rather than predictably reweighted by prior outcomes. Zhou et al. (2018) optimize sequential covariate balance without spillover or carryover inference. Li--Zhao (2026) provides the adaptive finite-population martingale template, but not dependent two-stage exposure scores. Li--Ding--Rubin (2018) and Lu et al. (2023) give static hard-rerandomization projection geometry. Li--Ding (2017), Shi--Ding (2026), and Tian--Yang--Ding (2025) supply finite-population Gaussian approximation tools, but not radial soft weighting of unbounded score quadratics on singular covariance support. Jizhou Liu (2026) covers static two-stage covariate-adaptive inference, He--Tchetgen Tchetgen (2026) covers broader static two-stage interference, and Liu--Shaikh--Zhong (2026) covers static saturation randomization tests; these current results sharpen the boundary around the proposed outcome-adaptive repeated-block theorem.
technical_internal_limitation: The launch is killed by any bounded legal triangular array for which \(\texttt{oeq:weighted-gaussian-transport}\) fails. Ordinary scalar Berry--Esseen convergence is insufficient because the covariance calculation uses a soft-weighted unbounded quadratic score. Exact enumeration over \(1{,}536\) assignments at \(G=n=4\) checked unbiasedness and the PSD-completion identity only; it is diagnostic evidence, not an asymptotic proof. Pair-probability concentration and the alternating-family uniform history bound remain explicit proof debts.
honest_scope: The estimand is a sustained two-period endpoint contrast under ordinary nonanticipation and an imposed lag-one finite-memory restriction; contemporaneous and carryover components are not separately identified. The population matrix \(P\) depends on unobserved potential-outcome scores through \(\beta_b\), so \(c^\top Pc>0\) is a theoretical characterization and is not claimed to be observable or screenable before deployment without a separate proxy or estimation theorem. The main asymptotics require both \(G\) and \(B\) to grow, predictable covariance stabilization, and \(\lambda_{\min}(\Omega_{\mathrm{RR}})>0\). When the soft tilt is switched off, the construction reduces to ordinary balanced two-stage randomization. The Yu--Ma--Liu market calibration and the Bojinov--Shephard trading experiment are prospective design consumers only; ten historical markets do not validate the growing-\(G\) Gaussian tilt formula.
